Question: What is the best way to get revenge on someone who broke your heart?
Answer: Work on yourself until you think the world is at your feet. Create some goals. Have some aspirations and work on them with all your capability, energy, and enthusiasm. No stepping back! Gain knowledge as much as you can. This will give you visibility in the crowd. Meet wonderful people and learn from them how you can groom. Confidence will come once you establish yourself in a career. So focus on building your career. Take care of your health and skin. It would be best if you glowed both in and out. Smile! This will break your opponent's heart into pieces. Don't waste your time thinking about punishing that person. It will take you nowhere. Understand that they were not suitable for you. So move on and focus on your life. The best thing I would do if I was deceived is forgive that person. I wouldn't wish ill for them. Because my energy is precious to me, I can't waste it thinking about people who could not value me. Life is too short. Live it with grace. Work on your happiness and live like a badass. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Question: How come I never learn lessons from mistakes?
Answer: I am currently pursuing my master's degree, and three months ago, I faced a practical exam. Unfortunately, due to time constraints and my child's illness, my preparation was not thorough. I left an important but lengthy theory unread, believing that the universe would favour me by not including it in the question paper. This overconfidence backfired when the exact theory appeared in the exam. Though I wrote it with my limited knowledge and also could expand it through my writing skill, the results were not upto par. Fortunately, I passed with the help of the viva. This experience left me somewhat disheartened. In December, I had exams again and this time, I studied well, tried to cover as much as I could. I refused to leave anything to luck. And my hard work paid off as I performed well in the exams. I have cultivated a determination to achieve my life goals. So the mistakes that I make become my greatest teacher. I don't want to repeat them. My aspirations hold great value and I am earnestly dedicated to reaching them. How come you never learn lessons from your mistakes? Perhaps because you haven't fully embraced and loved your life or developed a profound desire for improvement. The day you yearn for self-improvement, you will truly begin to learn from the mistakes that have hindered your growth. I wish you all the best on your journey. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Question: I want a strong comeback in life with my success in an exam which is in 3 months. What should I do?
Answer: Three months means 90 days that consists of 2,160 hours. Not bad! Make a daily routine and follow it vigorously. Try to utilize your time for your studies as much as you can. Aim for 6–7 hours of sleep every day to enhance concentration. Drink more water to keep yourself hydrated. Eat healthy and light. This will keep you active and focused. Give a break to all your social media accounts. Uninstall them from your phone. While studying, turn off the internet or keep the phone away. Read your notes thoroughly, write them and revise them quickly in every three days. There are three stages in our brain - When we read something, it enters our sensory memory, where it stays briefly. Repetition helps it transition to our short term memory (STM). After revising for a couple of days, it is stored in our long term memory (LTM), making it difficult to forget. Consider putting your friends, family and relationships on hold for three months to achieve better results. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: My boyfriend called me ugly during an argument then told me his friend thought I was ugly too. What do I do?
Answer: Recently I read an article written by Srinath Nalluri where he says - Red flags will remain red flags only, no matter how many good things take place in the relationship. And I agree with him. Some people lose their minds in anger, which is acceptable, but it doesn't provide them the right to demean others. Belittling your partner in the relationship is mental harassment. For me, it's a kind of crime because it gives a scar for a lifetime. I am ugly, average-looking or beautiful - didn't you analyze this before saying yes to me for the relationship? If not, you are mindless and act on an impulse. I can not be with you at all. Once, I was sitting with my relatives, and we discussed marriage. They talked about adjustment, which the wife must do because her husband is the one who ultimately cares about her. He is a man with lots of work stress in mind. If he shouts at his wife because of his frustration, the wife should understand him. Then only a marriage can work. And they concluded by saying that marriage is all about adjustment. This kind of adjustment? I bewildered. If marriages are based on give and take policy, then this should be implemented to love, respect, and compassion too. If you love and respect me, I will reciprocate the same or vice versa. By marrying you, I didn't give you authority to demean, belittle or hurt me, no matter how disturbed you are in your personal life. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Question: What is your "golden rule" when it comes to relationships?
Answer: Reciprocate. I believe in a relationship where both the parties are good at reciprocating. If I love someone, I want that person to respond to my love. If I care about them, they must show their concerns for me when I am in need. If I am available for them, I expect them to be equally available for me. If this reciprocation is not there, the relationship goes into darkness. We don't understand if our love is accepted or appreciated. Once we know our love has been accepted and cherished, we tend to give more. And the relationship thrives when the receiver returns the same gesture. I have witnessed many relationships becoming monotonous over time, and one partner blames the other, stating that they have become careless. Actually, they have not become careless; they have simply forgotten to reciprocate. So, learn to reciprocate. Give as much as you receive. One-sided effort makes a relationship stagnant. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu .
